solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cat lady's in pursuit of desire

indicators.note: following behind, so the lady's piece comes after the desire piece

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
read as 'lady is', giving HER, the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: A woman's pet cat chasing after what it longs for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady's' is 'lady is', so HER stands for the lady and 'in pursuit of' puts it after PANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big wild feline, a leopard or jaguar, so it is one kind of cat.

clue.text: Fife to get the better of Dundee at the end

parts.note: to pip someone is to beat them narrowly

indicators.note: only the final letter of the city name is used

explanation.surface: A football match in which Fife edges out Dundee late on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fife' looks like the Scottish county, beside Dundee, but it is the small flute. Fife and Dundee are neighbouring places in east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife is a small high-pitched flute, so it is a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Sauce from fish farm: am counting up bottles!

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
the words hold the letters inside them, as a bottle holds its contents

explanation.surface: A fish farm owner tallying jars of sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' holds MAMCOUN in 'farm am counting', and 'up' reads it backwards. Nuoc mam is Vietnamese.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuoc mam is the Vietnamese condiment made from fermented fish, a fish sauce.

clue.text: Did not relish being kept without date? Not half

indicators.note: without means outside, so the kept word goes around the half word

parts.note: had means kept or owned, as in had a dog

indicators.note: not half of the word survives, only its second half is kept

explanation.surface: Someone resenting being held without a date for release, and how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, not lacking. 'Not half' also reads as slang for very much.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is the strong form of not enjoying or liking it.

clue.text: Ruddy problem in retaining copper penny from former days

parts.note: the rub is the problem, as in Hamlet's there's the rub

indicators.note: the word in holds the copper symbol inside it

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper
D was the old penny before British decimalisation in 1971

explanation.surface: A dilemma involving copper coins from the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: RUB is the problem, as in Hamlet's there's the rub; D was the British penny before decimal coinage arrived in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubicund means reddish in the face, a high-coloured complexion.

clue.text: Hide away in corner of Greek island?

parts.note: SE, south-east, names a corner of a map or of a country
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone tucking themselves out of sight in a remote nook of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corner' is a compass corner, SE for south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it or stash it out of sight, the less common sense beside oozing.

clue.text: Southern European capital, not against producing pigment

indicators.note: not removes the against letter from the capital

parts.note: Vienna is the capital of Austria
V for versus means against

explanation.surface: A southern European capital opposing nothing while producing a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the V for versus; the leading S is a separate piece, not part of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, yellow-brown raw or reddish-brown when burnt, named after the Italian city.

clue.text: Be honest and firm with spy about end to espionage

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the spy's name goes round that final letter

parts.note: Donald Maclean was one of the Cambridge Five who spied for the Soviets, here given the Mc spelling

indicators.note: only the last letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A company being frank and resolute with an agent on how espionage finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Maclean was one of the Cambridge Five, British officials who spied for the Soviet Union; the setter uses the Mc spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for confessing or owning up, telling the whole truth.

clue.text: Intellectual encouraged absorbing sources of history and art, separately

indicators.note: separately means the two letters go in at different places, not as a pair
the encouraged word takes the two source letters into itself

parts.note: egged, as in egged on, means encouraged

indicators.note: sources are beginnings, so the opening letter of history is taken

parts.note: the source of art is its first letter, the sources of indicator covering both words

explanation.surface: A scholar spurred on by taking in both history and art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sources of' serves both history and art; 'separately' means the two letters go into EGGED at different points rather than as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal word for a highbrow, bookish person.

clue.text: Heard exact changes from an authoritative source

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A report that precise alterations came from someone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges HEARD EXACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex cathedra is Latin for 'from the chair', used of statements made with full official authority, as by the Pope.

clue.text: Drink surrounds most of historic feature of bar?

indicators.note: the drink word goes round the shortened historic word

parts.note: a potable is something fit to drink, so the noun means a drink

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for historic is dropped

parts.note: historic means old

explanation.surface: A drink wrapped around a relic of the past, as at some ancient inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' as a noun meaning something potable is the hard step; 'most of' drops the last letter of the historic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs commonly have a pool table, so it is a typical fixture of a bar; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Splendid and attractive without catch

indicators.note: the word for catch is removed from the word for attractive

parts.note: magnetic means attractive, drawing others in
a net is a catch, a haul of fish

explanation.surface: Praise for someone wonderful and charming but with no snag about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes NET from MAGNETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally 'magic' is an exclamation or adjective of praise meaning wonderful or terrific.

clue.text: The writer with dictionary encompassing translation of Chinese — there's improving stuff here

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself as ME

indicators.note: the abbreviation for dictionary goes around the rearranged letters
translating rearranges the following word's letters into a new form

explanation.surface: An author consulting a dictionary for a Chinese rendering, claiming it will be educational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, so ME; 'translation of' is the anagram signal for the word Chinese, held inside the dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine chest holds remedies that make you better, so it is where health-improving things are kept.

clue.text: Stop alcohol being added to German sweetmeat

parts.note: to stem is to stop a flow
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop spiking a German treat with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command, but it is the verb stem.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem ginger is preserved ginger root in syrup, eaten as a confection.

clue.text: Clock setting? Endless fluster one observed around Middle East

indicators.note: the shortened fluster word is seen placed round the abbreviation for the region
the last letter of the fluster word is dropped

parts.note: a tizz is a state of fluster or agitation

explanation.surface: Someone flustered checking their clock while abroad in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of the fluster word; 'observed around' sets it round the Middle East abbreviation before ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A time zone is a region that sets its clocks to one standard hour, so it governs how clocks are set.

clue.text: Variable land, fine after tilling to produce grape variety

parts.note: Z is a standard algebraic variable

indicators.note: tilling turns over soil, so the letters of the two words are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Ploughing a piece of fine land to grow a kind of wine grape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tilling' turns the land over, the anagram signal; 'after' is a link, the variable coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinfandel is a black wine grape grown widely in California.

clue.text: Parish officer's a busy one, controlling wayward lad

indicators.note: the busy creature holds the rearranged letters within it, as if keeping the lad in check

parts.note: the bee is proverbially busy

indicators.note: wayward suggests going astray, so the letters of lad are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bustling parish official keeping an unruly boy in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' scrambles the lad, and 'controlling' holds him inside the busy one. The 's is is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle was a minor church official of a parish, keeping order in services.

clue.text: Energetic person giving axe to bouncer

parts.note: to axe someone is to fire them from a job
a ball bounces

explanation.surface: A lively type sacking the nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' looks like a doorman but is a ball, and 'axe' is to sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireball is a person of great energy and drive, in the figurative sense of a blazing ball.

clue.text: Significance of word from Paris about soldiers

indicators.note: the French word goes round the word for soldiers

parts.note: mot is French for word
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: The meaning of a French word concerning troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Mot is French for word; 'about' puts the soldiers inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moment means importance or weight, as in a matter of great moment.

clue.text: Horse and bear without tail caged by fool

indicators.note: the shortened word is shut inside the fool word

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool

indicators.note: the last letter of the bear word is dropped

parts.note: to stand something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A horse and a tailless bear locked up by an idiot, like a circus gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is the verb, to put up with, not the animal; 'without tail' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild or half-wild horse of the American West.

clue.text: Red stuff beginning to cover area in two taverns

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used
the abbreviation for area sits between the two tavern words

parts.note: an inn and a bar are both taverns

explanation.surface: Some red substance beginning to coat a stretch of two pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the area abbreviation between the two taverns, after the first letter of cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is mercury sulphide, the source of vermilion, and its colour is a bright scarlet.

clue.text: Refuse maybe to buy son house — no time

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: the time word is removed from the house word

parts.note: a cottage is a small house
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Perhaps refusing to buy one's son a house, with no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as rubbish, but it is the verb. 'no' removes AGE from COTTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott goods is to refuse to purchase them as a protest; 'maybe' notes it can be other dealings too.

clue.text: A US Institute's upset about finally gaining mark of disgrace

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round that final letter
in a down entry upset turns the letters upside down, so they are reversed

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: only the last letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An American institute's upset over finally gaining a slur on its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A MITS into STIMA, which 'about' wraps round G, the end of 'gaining'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a badge of shame, a sign of social disapproval attached to someone.

clue.text: It lets you see again star in penalty shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A football or hockey highlight showing a star player's penalty kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like the penalty itself but is the anagram signal for STAR IN PENALTY.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant replay re-shows a moment of a televised game straight after it happens.

clue.text: Out of practice? Left for run, becoming vigorous

indicators.note: for means the left letter stands in place of the run letter

parts.note: rusty means out of practice
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone unpractised took a left turn instead of running and got energised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps R for L in RUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means full of healthy energy and strength, hearty and vigorous.

clue.text: Simple limits to mortgage rate

indicators.note: limits are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of each word are used

explanation.surface: Easy rules capping the interest on a home loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits to' takes ME and RE from 'mortgage rate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child, so it is plain or simple.

clue.text: Knocked back dope snatching a watch

indicators.note: backwards means the combined letters are read in reverse
the drug word grabs the letter a and holds it inside

parts.note: dope is a drug

explanation.surface: Someone downed a drug after stealing a wristwatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snatching' puts A inside DRUG for DRAUG, and 'Knocked back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard and to watch both mean to keep an eye on; a watch is also a sentry or guard.

clue.text: Former leader hosting guys in grand style

indicators.note: the grand and style pieces take the guys in between them

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand
tone means style or manner
lads are guys

explanation.surface: An ex-leader entertaining people in impressive fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' wraps grand and style round the guys; 'in' is a link. William Gladstone was a 19th-century British Prime Minister, four times in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone led Britain as Prime Minister in the Victorian era, so he is a past national leader.

clue.text: Artist with back trouble grabbing for one's finery

indicators.note: the artist's letters take hold of the abbreviation inside them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
EG, for example, means for one

indicators.note: back means the trouble word is read in reverse

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A painter with a bad back clutching at someone's fancy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist; 'back' reverses only the trouble word. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the robes and emblems of rank, so they are ceremonial dress and decoration.

clue.text: Recent issue might get this coverage, however coming in delayed

definitions.text: Recent issue might get this coverage

indicators.note: the however word enters the delayed word

parts.note: late means delayed
yet means however or nevertheless

explanation.surface: A recent edition of a magazine getting press coverage, even if it arrived late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recent issue' is a newborn baby, not a magazine edition: issue means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the set of clothes and bedding prepared for a newborn, who is a recent issue or offspring.
